remarks.text: Steinbeck continued: “And this I believe: that the free, exploring mind of the individual human is the most valuable thing in the world. And this I would fight for: the freedom of the mind to take any direction it wishes, undirected. And this I must fight against: any idea, religion, or government which limits or destroys the individual. This is what I am and what I am about. I can understand why a system built on a pattern must try to destroy the free mind, for that is one thing which can by inspection destroy such a system. Surely I can understand this, and I hate it and I will fight against it to preserve the one thing that separates us from the uncreative beasts. If the glory can be killed, we are lost.”
remarks.translation: 斯坦贝克继续写道："我坚信：个体人类自由探索的心灵，是世间最珍贵的存在。我愿为之奋斗的，是思想不受任何指引、随心所欲驰骋的自由。我必须反抗的，是任何限制或摧毁个体的思想、宗教或政府。这就是我的本质与使命。我能理解为何建立在固定模式上的体系必须试图摧毁自由思想，因为唯有自由思想能通过审视瓦解这种体系。我当然明白这一点，但我憎恶它，并将与之抗争到底，以守护那将我们与缺乏创造力的野兽区分开来的唯一特质。若这份荣光能被扼杀，我们便万劫不复。"

remarks.name: Garry Tan
remarks.role: President & CEO ycombinator —Founder garryslist—Creator of GStack & GBrain—designer/engineer who helps founders—SF Dem accelerating the boom loop
remarks.text:
“Our species is the only creative species, and it has only one creative instrument, the individual mind and spirit of a man. Nothing was ever created by two men. There are no good collaborations, whether in music, in art, in poetry, in mathematics, in philosophy. 

Once the miracle of creation has taken place, the group can build and extend it, but the group never invents anything. The preciousness lies in the lonely mind of a man.”

—John Steinbeck, East of Eden
remarks.translation: “我们这个物种是唯一具有创造力的物种，而它唯一的创造工具，就是个人的心智与精神。没有任何东西是由两个人共同创造出来的。无论是在音乐、艺术、诗歌、数学还是哲学中，都不存在良好的合作。一旦创造的奇迹发生，群体可以将其构建和扩展，但群体从不发明任何东西。珍贵之处在于一个人孤独的头脑。” ——约翰·斯坦贝克，《伊甸之东》

remarks.name: Matt Turck
remarks.role: VC at FirstMarkCap.  Host: MAD Podcast; Organizer: Data Driven NYC, Author: MAD Landscape.
remarks.text:
I don't understand what the tech industry doesn't understand about resistance against data centers. 

* AI is mostly built by coastal/tech elites who generally don't live near data centers; people near data centers don't trust them

* Trade jobs demand is welcome, but it's just for a few years during construction

* Communities don't want to be stuck with half-finished gigantic empty warehouses if the AI bubble bursts;  

* they don't find AI particularly helpful in their daily lives. 

* yes data centers run in close loops for water but elecriticy concerns are real and energy generation does have an impact 

Yes some NIMBYism but those concerns are not entirely unreasonable?  I'm obviously deeply pro-AI but dismissing concerns or thinking they're the result of some Chinese psyOps feels like another tone-deaf moment for the tech industry.  We need to do better.
remarks.translation:
我不太理解，科技行业为何对数据中心引发的抵触情绪如此不解。  
* AI主要由沿海/科技精英打造，他们大多不住在数据中心附近；而住在数据中心附近的人并不信任他们  
* 技术工种的需求固然受欢迎，但这仅限于建设期间的短短几年  
* 社区不希望AI泡沫破裂后，被半途而废的巨型空置仓库困住  
* 他们在日常生活中并未觉得AI有多大帮助  
* 没错，数据中心的水资源是闭环循环利用，但电力方面的担忧是真实存在的，能源生产确实会产生影响  
诚然，其中有些“邻避效应”，但这些担忧并非全无道理吧？  
我显然是深度支持AI的，但轻视这些担忧，或认为它们是某种中国心理战的产物，感觉又是科技行业一次脱离现实的反应。  
我们需要做得更好。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
Great post both if you’re driving AI in an enterprise or building for an enterprise. 

AI productivity gains are going to wildly vary - much wider than you think - because what you can do at the frontier is so significant if you fundamentally change your workflows to support agents. The challenge is that most people won’t or can’t naturally do this because of the complexity it entails.

Thus, a large amount of automation with agents is going to come from just getting agents wired up into a workflow that the user never ends up noticing or caring about:

“For everybody else, the work has to get done without them changing how they work, which means the AI goes into the background. Why do you need AI to be prompted by a human anyway? Just figure out what the most repetitive processes are, build agents in your existing systems of record that employees are used to”

This is the real work ahead for most enterprises right now that want to get significant gains from AI. A lot less “let a thousand flowers bloom” and more “pick off the 10 highest leverage things in the enterprise and apply automation to them”. There’s no real shortcut here.
remarks.translation: 无论您是在企业内推动AI应用，还是为企业打造AI解决方案，这篇帖子都极具价值。AI带来的生产力提升幅度将大相径庭——远超您的想象——因为如果您从根本上改变工作流程以支持智能代理，在前沿领域所能实现的成果将极为显著。挑战在于，大多数人不会或无法自然而然地做到这一点，因为这涉及到的复杂性太高。因此，大量基于智能代理的自动化将来自于将代理无缝接入工作流程，而用户最终甚至不会察觉或在意：“对于其他人来说，工作必须在不改变他们工作方式的前提下完成，这意味着AI要退居幕后。为什么AI非得由人来提示呢？只需找出最重复的流程，在员工已习惯的现有记录系统中构建代理即可。” 对于当下大多数希望从AI中获得显著收益的企业来说，这才是真正需要着手的工作。少一些“百花齐放”的思路，多一些“找出企业中10个杠杆效应最高的环节，并对其应用自动化”的做法。这里没有真正的捷径可走。
remarks.observation: 这条言论可作为 Agent 产品形态、协作方式或能力边界的观察入口；只代表公开观点，不作为公司事实主证据。

remarks.text:
Weird world we're moving to where AI is writing all code and will probably review all code soon too.

Humans I guess just brainstorm with AI to design the product and then test the product as a user?

Except AI will probably be the first user of most software so yeah don't know where this is all going.
remarks.translation: 我们正步入一个奇异的世界，AI将编写所有代码，并且很快可能也会审查所有代码。人类大概只能与AI一起头脑风暴来设计产品，然后以用户身份测试产品？不过，AI很可能成为大多数软件的首位用户，所以，真不知道这一切将走向何方。

remarks.name: Peter Yang
remarks.role: Practical AI tutorials and interviews for busy people
remarks.text:
The biggest bottleneck to building a great AI agent isn't the model.

It’s when teams:

→ Bury their agent in too much context
→ Don't give it tools to find what it needs
→ Try to cover too much vs. nail a few core use cases

In my next episode, Nan and Jacob from @Linear walked me through exactly how they built a production agent from idea to launch. Below's a picture of the product memo that started it all.

📌 Subscribe to get our full interview tomorrow: https://t.co/NSTj7ijxE0
remarks.translation: 构建一个优秀AI智能体的最大瓶颈并非模型本身，而是团队常常：→ 让智能体淹没在过多上下文中 → 不提供工具让它找到所需信息 → 试图覆盖太多功能，而非专注于几个核心用例 在我的下一期节目中，来自@Linear的Nan和Jacob向我详细展示了他们如何从创意到发布构建一个生产级智能体。下面是启动这一切的产品备忘录图片。📌 订阅以获取我们明天的完整访谈：https://t.co/NSTj7ijxE0
